title: Add monthly study summary, daily goal, study heatmap, task tags, embedded notes, and expanded reward shop

requirements.text: Add backend support for a Monthly Study Summary that returns, at minimum, (a) total study minutes for a selected month and (b) the best week (highest 7-day total) within that month, computed from the user’s recorded study sessions (Pomodoro + Custom timer + Stopwatch) already tracked by the app.
acceptanceCriteria: A new backend method exists to fetch a monthly study summary for a given month (and year if needed) for the caller.
Monthly totals include minutes from all supported study modes (Pomodoro, Custom timer, Stopwatch).
The returned summary includes a best-week value for that month based on a 7-day window fully contained within the month.
If the user has no study sessions in the selected month, the method returns zero totals and does not trap.

requirements.text: Add a Monthly Study Summary UI view in the authenticated experience that displays the selected month’s total minutes studied and the best week for that month, with a simple month selector (e.g., previous/next month).
acceptanceCriteria: The UI shows the selected month label and two metrics: total study minutes and best-week minutes.
The UI can switch between months and updates the displayed numbers accordingly.
Loading and empty states are handled with clear English text.
Data is fetched via React Query and remains consistent after new study sessions are recorded (relevant queries invalidate/refetch).

requirements.text: Add backend support for a Study-Day Heatmap calendar by exposing per-day study minutes for a recent window (at minimum: last 90 days), derived from the user’s recorded study sessions (all modes combined).
acceptanceCriteria: A new backend method exists to fetch per-day aggregated study minutes for the caller for a defined recent range (at minimum last 90 days).
Returned data includes an unambiguous day key (e.g., UTC day start timestamp or YYYY-MM-DD) and total minutes for that day.
Days with no study time are either omitted or included with 0 minutes, but the frontend can reliably render a continuous heatmap range without guessing.
The method does not trap for new users with no sessions.

requirements.text: Add a Study-Day Heatmap UI view (GitHub-style) that visualizes daily study minutes over the recent window (at minimum: last 90 days) using intensity levels, plus a legend that explains the intensity meaning in English.
acceptanceCriteria: A heatmap grid renders for the selected time window (at minimum last 90 days).
Each day cell’s intensity reflects the minutes studied that day; days with 0 minutes render as the lowest intensity.
Hover or click on a day shows an English tooltip/popover with the date and minutes studied.
The heatmap data is loaded via React Query and displays an appropriate loading state.

requirements.text: Add a configurable Daily Study Goal feature: persist a per-user daily goal (in minutes) in the backend user profile, and expose methods to get/update that goal for the caller.
acceptanceCriteria: User profile persistence supports a daily study goal value (minutes) for each user.
A backend method exists to update the caller’s daily goal minutes with basic validation (e.g., non-negative and reasonable upper bound).
A backend method (or existing profile fetch) allows the frontend to read the caller’s current daily goal minutes.
Existing users without a goal have a sensible default (e.g., 0 meaning ‘no goal set’) and the backend does not trap.

requirements.text: Add a Daily Goal progress bar UI that shows today’s studied minutes versus the user’s configured daily goal, and provide a simple UI control to set/update the daily goal (in minutes).
acceptanceCriteria: If the daily goal is set (> 0), the UI shows a progress bar with ‘X / Goal minutes’ in English and a percent completion.
If the daily goal is not set (0 or missing), the UI prompts the user in English to set a goal and does not show misleading progress.
Updating the goal triggers a backend update and the displayed goal/progress refreshes via React Query invalidation.
Today’s studied minutes include Pomodoro + Custom timer + Stopwatch and update after recording a session (via existing query invalidation patterns).

requirements.text: Add Task Categories/Tags: extend the task data model to support assigning one or more tags (text labels) to each task, and add backend methods to create/update tags on tasks and to list tasks with their tags for the caller.
acceptanceCriteria: Tasks can store tags (0..N) as text labels and return them in task reads.
Task create/update flows support setting tags without breaking existing tasks created before this feature.
A caller can update a task’s tags without affecting unrelated fields (title/description/subject/priority/completed).
If a migration/state upgrade is needed due to schema changes, it is implemented using the project’s conditional migration approach and does not wipe existing user data.

requirements.text: Add Task Tags UI: allow users to add/remove tags on tasks, and provide a simple filter to view tasks by a selected tag (including an ‘All’ view).
acceptanceCriteria: Task create/edit UI supports adding/removing tags with clear English labels.
The To-Do list can be filtered by a selected tag and returns to an ‘All’ view reliably.
Tag changes persist to the backend and the tasks list refreshes via React Query invalidation.
The UI behaves sensibly for tasks with no tags (still visible in ‘All’; excluded from specific-tag filters).

requirements.text: Add ‘Notes inside each task’: allow attaching an existing note to a task (by reference) and/or creating a new note from within the task edit flow, with backend persistence of the task↔note association.
acceptanceCriteria: A task can be associated with zero or more notes, and the association persists across reload and re-login.
From the task UI, a user can link an existing note to a task and unlink it later.
From the task UI, a user can create a new note and attach it to the task in the same flow.
Deleting a note that is linked to tasks does not break task rendering; tasks either drop the missing link or show a clear English ‘note not found’ fallback.

requirements.text: Add ‘Notes inside each reminder’: allow attaching an existing note to a reminder (by reference) and/or creating a new note from within the reminder edit flow, with backend persistence of the reminder↔note association.
acceptanceCriteria: A reminder can be associated with zero or more notes, and the association persists across reload and re-login.
From the reminders UI, a user can link/unlink existing notes to a reminder.
From the reminders UI, a user can create a new note and attach it to the reminder in the same flow.
Reminder notification behavior remains unchanged and does not duplicate due to note changes.

requirements.text: Expand the coin reward shop by adding additional purchasable items beyond backgrounds, with clear item listing, coin costs, purchase confirmation, and per-user permanent ownership so previously purchased items are not charged again when re-equipped/used.
acceptanceCriteria: The app shows an expanded shop list with at least one new item category beyond backgrounds (cosmetic/non-functional items are acceptable).
Each item has a clear English name, a coin cost, and an owned/unowned state.
Purchasing an item deducts coins once, persists ownership for the user, and prevents repurchase charges for already-owned items.
Coin balance and any relevant ownership queries are refreshed via React Query invalidation after purchase.
If the user does not have enough coins, the purchase is blocked and an English error message is shown.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor (all logic in backend/main.mo).
Do not edit files under frontend/src/components/ui or any paths listed as immutable in SYSTEM_CONTEXT.
Use English for all new user-facing UI text.
If schema/state changes require migration, follow the project’s conditional migration policy and preserve existing user data.
nonGoals: Implementing third-party authentication beyond Internet Identity.
Adding real-time features (WebSockets, push notifications, chat).
Integrating external databases or non-Motoko backend services.
Changing or removing any existing timetable, streak, reminders, tasks, level, coins, or background functionality beyond what is necessary to add the requested features.
